fixes.name: Chained assignment and Copy-on-Write
fixes.what: Recognize why chained indexing like df[df.x > 0]['y'] = 1 does not change the original DataFrame: since pandas 3.0, Copy-on-Write is the default, so every indexing result behaves as a copy and chained assignment never writes back (older versions sometimes did and showed SettingWithCopyWarning instead). Assign safely in one step with df.loc[rows, col] = value, or work on an explicit .copy().
fixes.why: Since pandas 3.0, Copy-on-Write is the default and SettingWithCopyWarning has been removed. Chained assignment now always fails to update the original, so 'can fail' and the warning describe the old behaviour.
The point says pipelines prevent leakage, and that makes no sense without first knowing what data leakage is.
The end-to-end project tunes the pipeline with cross-validation, which is the grid search taught in p127. p125 alone only scores a model and does not tune it.
train_test_split returns four arrays that are unpacked in one assignment (X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = ...), so it relies on tuple unpacking.
The point asks the learner to plot learning and validation curves, which needs basic matplotlib plotting.
Seeing how feature scaling changes k-nearest neighbors needs the scalers, and the reason distance-based models need them, taught in p105.
Computing accuracy compares a model's predictions with the true labels, so it needs fit and predict first.
Building a Series or DataFrame starts with import pandas as pd. Every other library entry point on the map (p52, p67, p88) needs p37, and this one should too.

verdict: The map is sound. Its scope, order and route fit the goal well. The fixes update one point that described pandas behaviour from before Copy-on-Write became the default, and fill in a few missing prerequisite links, mainly in the machine-learning topics.
